newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: One-day strike disrupts Portuguese rail services.
newsitem.headline: One-day strike disrupts Portuguese rail services.

text.p: A one-day strike to protest against the restructuring of loss-making state railway company CP-Caminhos de Ferro Portugueses disrupted goods and passenger services across Portugal on Friday, a union spokesman said.
"Many trains have been cancelled or delayed in Lisbon, Oporto, Sintra, Setubal and elsewhere," Jose Manuel Oliveira of the Federation of Portuguese Railway Workers' Unions told Reuters.
"Since midnight no goods trains have been circulating," he added. "We are protesting against the lack of guarantees for jobs in the restructuring of the railways."
Oliveira estimated that about 80 percent of Portugal's 15,000 railway workers were involved in the strike.
CP officials were not immediately available to comment.
Portugal is overhauling its creaking railway system and inviting private contractors to operate some lines in a crusade to boost efficiency and slash losses.
Under-Secretary for Transport Antonio Guilhermino Rodrigues told Reuters in April that the restructuring plan would not lead to dismissals.
